1.a4 b6 2.d4.strategy: White claims the centre at once, as the opening itself has not, and gives the c1-bishop its diagonal. Black's planned fianchetto on the long diagonal finds the centre already held by a solid pawn that White can support with natural development. It is the most sensible way to use the tempo.

1.a4 b6 2.d4 d5.strategy: Black answers the centre pawn with a pawn of its own and keeps the position balanced and closed. It blocks the d-file, but the pawn is only guarded by the queen and so ties it down.
